[TASK: ARCHITECTURAL RELIGHTING & STATIC RECONSTRUCTION]
Transform the reference photogrammetry plate into a razor-sharp, photorealistic architectural image.
Keep the reference plate's exact composition: every edge, horizon line, and object position stays where it is.

MANDATORY TRANSFORMATION RULES:
1. PLANAR RECTIFICATION & GEOMETRY LOCK: Treat the reference image as an immutable spatial coordinate frame. Eliminate all 3D mesh polygon wobble, melted facades, and distorted rooflines. Plumb all vertical walls to true gravity vertical. Render the specific materials, coursing, window types, and roof forms named in the SCENE section below with sharp, correct detail.
2. STATIC DECLUTTERING (MANDATORY): COMPLETELY ERASE all transient vehicles, parked cars, delivery vans, pedestrians, and temporary street clutter from the seed image. Repaint the ground plane with the authentic surfacing, kerbs, and pavement named in the SCENE section below.
3. BOTANICAL PHENOLOGY & CANOPY INTEGRITY: Overwrite all raw 3D mesh blob foliage with authentic seasonal canopy structures matching the target date. Zero green summer foliage during dormant/autumn/winter periods:
   - Date-Grounded Phenology (September): Fully expanded late-summer canopy volumes displaying mature deep olive and forest greens, with early faint chlorosis/yellowing on select branch tips; zero leaf drop.
- Botanical Taxa:
  * Overstory Groves & Mall Borders: American Elm (*Ulmus americana*), Pin Oak (*Quercus palustris*), White Oak (*Quercus alba*), and American Sycamore (*Platanus occidentalis*).
  * Perimeter Plantings: Red Maple (*Acer rubrum*), London Planetree (*Platanus × acerifolia*), and Sweetgum (*Liquidambar styraciflua*).
  * Turf Cover: Dense, high-durability sod composition of Kentucky Bluegrass (*Poa pratensis*) and Tall Fescue (*Festuca arundinacea*), clipped to uniform height across the undulating knoll.
4. OPTICAL DEPTH: Sharp focus across the entire frame, near to far. No blur, no depth-of-field falloff, no vignetting.

[SOLAR & ATMOSPHERIC LIGHTING OVERRIDE]
SOLAR RELIGHTING DIRECTIVE (3000K Dusk / late sunset low-angle amber golden hour with elongated cast shadows):
- SUN POSITION IN SCREEN SPACE: Sun is at the LEFT edge of the frame, roughly level with the view direction (True Azimuth 276.4°, Elevation 3.7°).
- FACADE ILLUMINATION: camera-facing facades receive grazing light and read as half-lit; left-facing walls are brightly lit and right-facing walls are in deep shadow.
- CAST SHADOW DIRECTION: long lateral cast shadows run horizontally across the ground to the RIGHT.
- CAST SHADOW LENGTH: Cast shadows are more than twelve times the height of the object casting them: extremely long, running off the edge of the frame.
- SHADOW OVERWRITE RULE: MANDATORY: Erase every cast shadow present in the reference plate before relighting. Render all previously shadowed ground and facades as if that shadow never existed, then cast entirely new shadows so that long lateral cast shadows run horizontally across the ground to the RIGHT. Every shadow must be angled toward the RIGHT; a shadow running straight up or straight down the frame is wrong. Do not retain, tint, or reuse any shadow from the reference plate.
- WEATHER/SKY: Crisp clear sky with direct solar exposure.

[SCENE GEOMETRY & AUTHENTIC LITHICS]
Monumental 555-foot hollow masonry obelisk with four precisely plumb, tapering ashlar faces terminating in an equilateral pyramidal capstone. Lower shaft section constructed of pale cream Cockeysville calcitic marble, shifting at the 152-foot line to lighter Lee Massachusetts dolomitic marble with Maine granite core backing. Base surrounded by a wide circular plaza of concentric flame-finished gray granite and Pennsylvania bluestone pavers, ringed by 50 fixed stainless steel flagpoles. Surrounding landscape consists of a manicured undulating turf knoll of Kentucky bluegrass intersected by curved asphalt and crushed-granite walkways. Adjacent modern museum structure exhibits a three-tiered inverted corona of dark bronze-finished cast-aluminum lattice over recessed structural glazing. Surrounding city background comprised of Neoclassical federal administrative blocks clad in smooth Indiana limestone ashlar, colossal Ionic and Doric colonnades, multi-lite rectangular sash windows, and pitched hipped roofs of red terracotta barrel tile. Mature dense tree canopies of Ulmus americana, Quercus palustris, and Platanus occidentalis in full early-September deep green foliage bordering formal lawns and paved avenues. Surface textures range from weathered crystalline stone and fine hydraulic lime mortar joints to smooth vitreous roof tile, honed paving bands, and aggregate roadway asphalt. Zero dynamic clutter, vehicles, or pedestrians.
